questions.prompt: Which sources should the stricter plan-value gate cover?
questions.description: Current code only annotates adapter/discovered plans locally, while user-created and custom directories bypass local annotation and Convex also bypasses custom/user metadata in visibility heuristics. The Convex table already contains low-value custom-dir and cloud/user-created rows, so this choice determines how comprehensive the fix should be.
questions.recommendedAnswer: Apply the same canonical plan-value gate to every inbound path before indexing or syncing: adapter scans, project/discovered dirs, custom dirs, user-created local plans, cloud create/upload/publish, and cloud edits. Preserve explicit short checklist plans, but reject/prune empty, code-only, log/report/session, prompt-only, and heading-only content.

questions.prompt: How should existing low-value rows in Convex be handled?
questions.description: A dev-table sample found 866 plan rows, 132 already invisible by current server heuristics, and additional custom-dir/autosession rows that look like CI logs, empty outputs, or short scratch files. Current code hides many of these but leaves them in the plans table unless a local lowValue metadata payload is later synced for the same localPlanId.
questions.recommendedAnswer: Add a dry-run-first cleanup/backfill path that classifies every existing Convex plan with the canonical gate, reports counts/reasons/source breakdown, then deletes/prunes low-value rows and related data using deletePlanRelatedData after approval. Do not rely on UI hiding alone.

questions.prompt: How strict should the definition of a real plan be?
questions.description: The current heuristic accepts structured headings, checklists, ordered steps, action bullets, explicit proposed_plan blocks, and some future-plan language, but misses code-dominated answers and duplicates logic between shared and Convex implementations.
questions.recommendedAnswer: Use a strict allowlist-style classifier: content must have explicit plan structure or enough actionable planning prose, while code-dominated/code-only documents, empty rows, heading-only docs, prompt-only requests, execution reports, review outputs, tool/system logs, and generic conversations are low-value. Keep minimal checklists like '- [ ] Fix login bug' as valid.

questions.prompt: What verification should be required before considering this resolved?
questions.description: The implementation can include deterministic unit tests, adapter/rescan/sync tests, Convex visibility/prune tests, and an audit command over current Convex data.
questions.recommendedAnswer: Require unit tests for new low-value shapes, service tests proving all scan/rescan paths annotate or exclude correctly, CLI/daemon sync tests proving low-value plans are not sent except explicit prune cleanup, Convex tests/validation for publish/edit and cleanup behavior, and a dry-run audit report against the current plans table showing the targeted rows before deletion.
